text:
Nora Li: hi team  quick onboarding questions before I start Mon. Two tricky ones: (1) Im coming off a US contractor engagement that had an HSA contribution. If I elect HSA pre-tax here, can contributions be backdated to cover the month I start? Also how do HSA payroll deductions work if my bank is registered in Singapore (SGD acct)? (2) Im eligible for the commuter pre-tax benefit but my commute will be occasional and Id like to enroll mid-month. Is there a pro-rate window or do I wait until next month? Also Monday is a bank holiday in my location  will that push any of this?

Maya (People Ops): welcome Nora! :wave: Short answers: (1) HSA elections cannot be backdated; coverage/election effective date is your benefits effective date (your start date). Pre-tax payroll deductions start the first pay period after enrollment processes through Workday (usually within one pay cycle). For SG bank acct: payroll can deduct USD HSA contributions from your USD payroll and then remit to the HSA custodian; we dont direct debit from SGD accounts. If you need local currency conversion for reimbursements we can discuss but HSA accounts must be a US-qualified custodian.

Maya (People Ops): (2) Commuter pre-tax: if you enroll mid-pay-period we prorate the deduction based on enrollment date for that payrun. You can opt in via the commuter portal; enroll before the payroll cutoff (Thursday 12:00 local) to catch the current payrun. Holiday: company-observed holidays dont change benefit effective date; they can delay bank settlement for direct deposit if your local bank is closed.

Jasmin (Payroll): adding payroll mechanics: HSA deductions are taken as pre-tax payroll deductions from the gross USD pay. If you want contributions to start immediately, enroll on Day 1 and complete any beneficiary forms. For bank issues: if your SGD account is set as primary, convert your payroll to USD direct deposit to HSA is not supported  we recommend keeping a US bank for HSA flows or using the HSA custodians web portal for manual funding. Reimbursements from HSA are done by the HSA custodian directly to you, not via payroll.

Marco (Benefits): HSA eligibility: ensure you arent enrolled in other disqualifying coverage (like an FSA thats limited purpose). If you had prior year funds from contractor period, those remain in your former HSA; you can still contribute to a new HSA if eligible. We dont backdate employer contributions.

Nora Li: got it re: HSA. Quick follow-up  what about FSA (dependent care)  can I elect it mid-year? I might have childcare bills from my relocation month and wondered if retro claims are allowed for pre-enrollment dates if the expense happened after my start date but before payroll processed enrollment.

Marco (Benefits): Dependent Care FSA: you must be enrolled for the period when the expense was incurred. If the expense occurred after your benefits effective date but before payroll processed enrollment, you can file a claim and well review for eligibility; often we can make a manual exception if docs show date-of-service after your start date. Upload receipts to benefits claims portal and tag "newhire-fsa". Include service date and provider info.

Jasmin (Payroll): for the prorated commuter and any mid-month FSA/benefit changes, note that payroll runs have cutoffs. If the benefit change posts after cutoff we process it on next run and then do any necessary manual adjustments on the following run. That sometimes shows as an "adjustment" line on paystub.

Nora Li: thanks! last tiny one  my offer mentioned PTO accrual starts on day one but I start the day before a regional bank holiday. Does that holiday reduce my first period accrual? Also any paperwork I should sign to avoid delays in bank deposit because my SG bank uses an IBAN-like number?

Maya (People Ops): PTO accrual: we prorate based on start date; a company-observed holiday that falls within your first pay period does not reduce your accrual entitlement. Youll see prorated days on your first paystub. Bank: send payroll a DM with your IBAN/Swift and a screenshot of a bank statement or a voided deposit slip to pre-validate. If the bank rejects direct deposit we can issue a single manual payment while we resolve routing.

onboard-bot: :link: Newhire benefits checklist updated: complete HSA enrollment, commuter enrollment (if desired), upload childcare/relocation receipts (for FSA), DM payroll bank validation. See https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/x/NewHireBenefits for region notes.

Nora Li: perfect, thanks everyone. Ill enroll Day 1 and DM payroll the bank screenshot now. Appreciate the clarity!
